title: Quantized slab pinning for ultra-long-context memory profiles (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Evan Park
description: Goal: Design and implement model-specific slab pinning and quantized-slab memory profiles that reduce GPU OOMs and improve latency for ultra-long-context workloads across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants. The feature introduces: (1) per-model/per-variant slab pinning policies that preferentially reserve GPU device memory for quantized KV slabs and activation slabs for layers sensitive to precision; (2) a quantization-sensitivity map built from offline calibration runs that guides which slabs may be stored in 4-bit/8-bit vs 16-bit to trade off fidelity vs footprint; (3) an eviction/fallback policy that integrates continuous batching heat signals and per-token hotness to avoid evicting high-reuse slabs during bursty long-sequence generation. This ticket spans offline calibration, runtime allocator changes, and integration with the batching and KV cache manager. Metrics: reduce OOM rate on 64k+ context runs by >= 70% for targeted models, keep p95 generation latency within 10% of baseline for long-tail batch sizes, and reduce average memory headroom variance across GC cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model profile artifacts produced for Llama-2-70b, Mistral-7B-Instruct longctx, and Qwen-14B-ext with quantization-sensitivity maps and slab pin priorities.
Runtime implements slab pinning flags: PIN_ALWAYS, PIN_IF_HOT, PIN_PREFER_QUANT and respects them across allocation/compaction cycles.
Eviction policy extended to consider continuous-batch hotness score and quantization penalty; validated via unit tests and end-to-end perf runs.
Benchmark run on nightly cluster shows >=70% reduction in OOM for 64k/128k sequences on targeted models and p95 latency impact <=10% vs current baseline.
PRs merged, design doc + calibration data uploaded to Drive, and rollout plan scoped with feature flag and telemetry dashboard entries.
implementation_notes: Calibration harness: create a short pipeline that runs representative long-context prompts and collects per-layer activation magnitude, forward/reverse reuse counts, and token reuse heat maps. Store results as CSV and a compact JSON map consumed by the allocator.

Representation: quantization-sensitivity map is a list of layer ids -> sensitivity score [0..1]. Low-score layers safe to store in 4-bit KV slabs; high-score keep at 16-bit activations. Default thresholds: <=0.25 -> 4-bit, 0.25-0.6 -> 8-bit, >0.6 -> 16-bit. Tune per-model empirically.

Allocator changes: add slab pin metadata to the slab descriptor; during placement prefer device-local pinned slabs. On compaction, skip PIN_ALWAYS slabs and consider PIN_IF_HOT only if cumulative hotness < eviction threshold.

KV manager integration: extend continuous batching router to emit per-request suffix hotness that contributes to slab hotness counters; decay counters over time windows aligned to typical conversational turn durations.

Fallback: when memory pressure triggers, we attempt (1) demote quantized slabs to lower precision only if sensitivity allows, (2) spill non-pinned slabs to host memory asynchronously, (3) selectively drop prefix KV entries based on token-level last-use timestamps as a last resort.

Testing: unit tests for slab metadata correctness, integration tests for longctx generation with synthetic workloads, and chaos tests that trigger high-concurrency continuous batching to validate eviction choices.
Telemetry: emit slab residency events, demotion events, and rejection rates. Add cost/latency rollup on per-model dashboards for the new config.
